independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session ec211475 (invocation task T-DG5-RG-SEC-R1). I authored no implementation in the DG5 scope. The P5 product is by solution-architect, backend-workflow-engineer, kpi-benefits-engineer, frontend-ux-engineer and transformation-analyst (docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/). The acceptance suites in the candidate are by qa-verifier, and the merges and the D-184 re-gate commit are by delivery-orchestrator.

Contract note: the assignment file names its task 'T-DG5-REV-SEC-R5', while the invocation reference names T-DG5-RG-SEC-R1. Everything else in the assignment (candidate, round 1, my id range F-DG5-100 to F-DG5-119, the paths) is consistent, so I followed it and use the invocation's run id verbatim.

My only writes are evidence under docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/code-security/round-1/, this record and its findings sidecar. Builds, static checks and all test runs used a disposable clone ($TMPDIR/rv, `git clone --shared`, not shallow, at freeze commit 53bd2d1) and disposable PostgreSQL 16.13 clusters on ports 26510, 26530 and 26550-26556. The clone was sparse: it left out docs/delivery/{test-evidence,handbacks,runs}, which are outside the candidate manifest, because the shared disk had 2.7 GB free and a full copy hit ENOSPC. My disposable repro tests were copied into the clone, run and deleted. The clone's git status was clean afterwards, and the clone and clusters were removed (46-cleanup.log). The validators and candidate.mjs ran read-only in the repository tree.

HEAD was 53bd2d1 when I started. During my run the runner auto-committed the domain reviewer's run evidence as e1b45a5 (docs/delivery only; candidate ID unchanged, 47-head-moved.log). I did not open any of those files. I formed my verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-1 record, and I have read none.

Confirm that the freeze commit adds only delivery records to source 270ebbf. Confirm that, outside docs/delivery, the re-gate source 270ebbf is byte-identical to the old branch head ac68d1b (D-184).

checks_run.actual:
The assignment hash matches (54384413128b6dded16e51ee97473e49142c6148e2ced9d4cf7f23c382b27d69). HEAD was 53bd2d1 (the round-1 freeze commit; its parent is source 270ebbf). Between 270ebbf and 53bd2d1 there are only the three round-1 assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json. `git diff --stat ac68d1b 270ebbf -- . ':!docs/delivery'` is empty, so the product is byte-identical to the old branch head, as D-184 states.

checks_run.expected: AUD gets 403 on every well-formed P5 write, and 404 only for a record that does not exist, with nothing written but a denial. No ADM caller gets a 2xx on a transformation-scoped operation, except where an ADR grants it.
checks_run.actual:
Every run exits 1 by design, because the sweep asserts the strict expectation and reports the deviations, which I then judged one by one. Final run 4: 296 of 301 tests pass, and the 5 that 'fail' are these:

(a) AUD previewFormula: 400, because it is not a write. formula-preview.ts:3-6 says it writes nothing and needs only a session and CSRF.

(b) ADM runJobNow (automation.tick_daily): 202. This is the intended ADM_TECH job operation (REQ-S12-022: TL/TO/AUD/ADM_METHOD get 403), not transformation-scoped.

(c-e) ADM_METHOD: 200 on listTransformationConfigPins, listConfigPinHistory and listMethodologyMigrations. ADR-0040 §9 (line 84) grants exactly these reads (methodology.read) to ADM_METHOD, which plans and executes migrations. This is designed, so I make it an observation, not a finding.

Final totals:
- AUD: 403 on 70 writes; 404 on 19 writes whose synthetic record id does not exist (no write; only the denial audit or none).
- ADM: 0 transformation-scoped 2xx; 40/40 reads are 403/404.
- ADM_METHOD writes: 0 2xx.

Run 2 also showed that 9 writes shape-validate an empty body before authorization (AUD 400 'validation', for example createFormDraft, the procedure step writes, decideApprovalRouteStep, closeGateCondition and decideKpiRestatement). With well-formed bodies (runs 3 and 4), all 9 give AUD 403 or 404. A body-shape 400 discloses only the public contract, so this is an observation. In run 1, 18 deviations came from my own malformed code params (UUIDs for elementType, questionCode and jobCode).

checks_run.command: git diff e70ac02f63cd1f42487cfa4dae73f68e933da015..270ebbf7477664cb17202ee2c32ac49c6f36c5ce -- apps packages; reading the files cited in 50-source-review.md
checks_run.expected: Every mutation is server-authorized at commit time, validated, If-Match guarded and audited. SoD holds at the API and in the database. There is no IDOR, no human-only automation and no demo binding in production.
checks_run.actual:
No defect found here.

Exports: 403 before the body for a caller without export.create anywhere (jobs.ts:298). Grants are reloaded in the write transaction (:346). The idempotency key is UNIQUE and replay-safe. Read, download and cancel are requester-only, with transformation.read re-checked (ownJob, :177; others 404). The store keys are opaque UUID paths confined to the root (storage.ts:90), with nosniff, private and no-store on download.

Studio SoD: the requester and every recorded contributor are refused at the API (reviews.ts:339) and by the 0097 constraint (:222). The reviewer is never AUD or a technical admin.

Approvals: an ADM approver role is refused at publish and in the database (ADR-0039 ME05/06). routedApproverOf honours approver_configured.

Procedures: 0096:57 allows exactly NULL -> T for a pending step of an active org-scope intake, to its capture_intake output. authorizeStepWrite (steps.ts:502) tries the instance scope, then T.

Attachments and bulk edit: the record and the evidence must both be in the URL's transformation (attachments.ts:207). Bulk edit locks in record-id order (bulk.ts:234), all-or-nothing.

Automation: scope first, then the identity (identity.ts:60). The database refuses approval or Finance codes on service identities (0074:233) and human-only actions on versions and results (0074:492). The dry run is read-only and rolled back (dry-run.ts:276).

Demo isolation: the dev binding needs AUTH_MODE=dev and not production (cli.ts:53, load.ts:196). No access administrator can grant themselves a role (assignments.ts:108).

Observations: the dry run's plan returns recipientUserIds of the sample's target transformation to the ADM_METHOD configurer without a transformation.read check (automation-actions.ts:129). ADR-0043 §1/§4/§8 design it that way: the org methodology admin configures transformation-scope rules, and the dry run returns target and assignee. The ADM_METHOD pin and migration reads are by ADR-0040 §9.

checks_run.procedure: Mechanically check the outbox registry: every OUTBOX_EVENT_SCHEMAS type has a consumer queue and every queue-mapped type has a schema, and every event-type literal at a product write site is registered. Mechanically check the advisory-lock registry: no duplicate class id, and every 7302xx literal used by the worker or packages (which import no API code) is registered. Read the relay's handling of an unregistered type, the export runner's attempts, and the engine's once-keys.
checks_run.command: node repro/outbox-registry.mjs; node repro/advisory-locks.mjs (from the clone root, Node 24 type stripping); reading apps/worker/src/relay.ts, reports/export-runner.ts and automation/engine.ts
checks_run.expected: The registries are consistent. An unregistered type never stalls later events. Every job is exactly once.
checks_run.actual:
Outbox: 26 schema types and 26 queue-mapped types; none without a queue and none without a schema. 22 event-type literals at write sites, all registered (40-outbox-registry.log, exit 0). Both writers (jobs/outbox.ts enqueueOutboxEvent and worker kit.ts) refuse an unregistered type at enqueue. The relay records a bad row (attempts + 1, last_error) and ends its round; after maxPublishAttempts it skips the row, so it delays later events but never stalls them (relay.ts:70).

Locks: 39 classes, no duplicate. The P5 classes 730250-730271 are listed. Every worker or package literal (730228-730271) is registered (44-advisory-locks.log, exit 0).

The export runner stores per attempt (`<job>-a<n>`, export-runner.ts:336), cleans up earlier attempts and refuses files over 200 MiB. The engine's UNIQUE automation_execution_once_key and per-action result keys back the lock. The replay ×3 tests (A13D, a13-jobs-rerun) passed in both integration runs.

checks_run.command: ls packages/db/migrations; grep GRANT/DISABLE/ENABLE/CONSTRAINT; node repro/migration-gap-order.mjs (from the clone root)
checks_run.expected: Forward-only and safe on every database, with guards and audit coverage. 0094's disable is contained.
checks_run.actual:
89 files apply cleanly in both integration runs. No P5 table grants DELETE to mth_app. Snapshot content, hash and context are immutable (0080:177), and the children are append-only. form_record_type and form_source_field are SELECT-only for mth_app (0068:45, :110). 0094 disables gate_instance_row_guard and audit_required inside its own transaction under the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock of ALTER TABLE, backfills only the new column, and re-enables both before commit (0094:27, :40); I accept this under ADR-0039 C2. 0096 is as described in SEC-R1-13.

Defect F-DG5-100 (Low, non-mandatory): the P5 ids 0066, 0067, 0073, 0077-0079, 0083 and 0084 are unused (planned gaps). The runner applies every pending file in lexical order and refuses only changed checksums and unknown applied files (migrate.ts:95, :159). seed.test.ts:767 admits any id up to 0099. The repro shows that a later 0066_p6_example.sql on an upgraded database is pending, with nothing refused. It would run 90th there but 66th on a fresh database, so the two diverge (41-migration-gap-order.log, exit 0). There is no effect on the candidate's own files.

Neither affects an assigned acceptance clause as written, and neither is blocking.
